d: A tough sheet of deep fascia stretched between the ischiopubic rami. It separates the deep perineal pouch above from the superficial pouch below, and the urethra and vagina pass through it.

The membranous layer of superficial fascia in the perineum. It attaches to the ischiopubic rami and the back edge of the perineal membrane and continues as dartos and Scarpa fascia, so it steers leaked urine forward.
Also called Alcock canal: a tunnel in the obturator fascia on the side wall of the ischioanal fossa. It carries the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels toward the perineum.
The wavy line in the anal canal where hindgut endoderm meets the ectoderm of the anal pit. The lining, blood supply, nerves and lymph drainage all change across it.
The fibromuscular knot of the perineum between the anal canal and the vagina or penile bulb. The perineal muscles and external anal sphincter anchor to it, and deeper obstetric lacerations tear it.

A connection between portal and caval veins. At the anorectal junction the superior rectal veins (portal) meet the middle and inferior rectal veins (caval), so in portal hypertension blood diverts there and swells rectal varices. The other classic sites are the lower esophagus (esophageal varices) and the umbilicus (caput medusae).
The first lymph node that receives drainage from a tumor. It is found with blue dye or a radiotracer and biopsied. If it is free of cancer, a full lymph node dissection can usually be avoided.
